title: Quenched Peruvian Duck-Confit-Leg Cazuela
description: A yeasty, crispy, and satisfying Peruvian brunch dish featuring slow-cooked duck confit leg. Perfect for a weekend morning.
instructions: In a large cazuela, combine duck confit leg, onion, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and yeast.
Deglaze the pan with apricot juice and white wine (if using).
Add chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and let cool to room temperature.
Once cooled, whisk together flour and water to make a dough.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes and shape into a round loaf.
Place the loaf in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Place the loaf in the oven and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the bread is baking, boil the Peruvian corn until tender.
To assemble, slice the bread into thick rounds and top each round with a duck confit leg, boiled corn, and a sprinkle of scallions.
